html:
SMTO-EXE-0154 — A desktop step took too long and was stopped

GUID: 7f5333ef-3f90-5033-8d3b-fdf92fe126f6
Slug: ui-operation-timeout
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO was waiting to work in an app on the Gateway's computer, but the step ran out of time before any click or typing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the Gateway's computer and close any pop-up, dialog or loading screen that is covering or freezing the app. SMTO waits for the app to answer, and a blocked or busy app makes the step run out of time.
  2. Make sure that computer is awake and unlocked, then ask SMTO in the conversation to try the step again. A sleeping or locked screen stops the app from answering in time; nothing was sent, so trying again is safe.
  3. If the app's window or list is very large, ask SMTO to look at only one part of it, such as a single panel or dialog. Reading a huge window can take longer than the time allowed for one step.

What success looks like

  • The step finishes and SMTO reports in the conversation what it found or did.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway's computer, noting which app was open. If SMTO later says a result is unknown, check the app before letting it repeat anything.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Desktop UI request reached its deadline (timeout_ms, default 10 s or 30 s for visual input, at most 60 s) at a checkpoint before any native input was dispatched.

What this means

  • A UI checkpoint or outer wait reached its deadline before a mutation had begun; if native mutation had begun, the service instead retains unknown outcome and keeps the input gate until return. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • A UI checkpoint or outer wait reached its deadline before a mutation had begun; if native mutation had begun, the service instead retains unknown outcome and keeps the input gate until return.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect timeout, mutation-start facts and gate state; distinguish an unstarted action from a possibly active native call.

How to fix it

  • Check the target application for modal dialogs, hangs or a locked session, then narrow the request (window_id, ancestor_ref, max_nodes, max_depth) or set a larger timeout_ms up to 60000. This receipt has executed=false; if any related receipt shows effect_unknown, reconcile it with ui.snapshot or ui.element before repeating.
  • Inspect current state; if an effect is unknown, do not repeat the action. Narrow the scope or choose a bounded longer timeout.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect current state; if an effect is unknown, do not repeat the action. Narrow the scope or choose a bounded longer timeout.

How to verify the fix

  • The original call is settled and its gate released before a new justified operation.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
